title: Cell-free lysate (E. coli) preparation with sonication
author: Nadanai Laohakunakorn
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8nthven
materials: Prepare all materials for bacterial culture This protocol will make 200 mL of culture to yield around 1 mL of lysate with a protein concentration of around 40 - 80 mg/mL.
Finally, carefully discard as much supernatant as possible.
Preparation of 1M stock solutions of tris acetate, magnesium glutamate, and potassium glutamate

steps.title: Prepare Buffer A and Stocks
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary stock solutions and Buffer A.

substeps.instruction: Make 1M tris acetate stock: Weigh 12.11 g tris base (121.14 g/mol), add to 100 mL deionized water, and adjust to pH 8.2 with acetic acid.
Make 1M magnesium glutamate stock: Weigh 38.86 g magnesium glutamate (388.61 g/mol) and add to 100 mL deionized water.
Make 1M potassium glutamate stock: Weigh 20.32 g potassium glutamate (203.23 g/mol) and add to 100 mL deionized water.

Prepare Buffer A (10 mM tris acetate, 14 mM magnesium glutamate, 60 mM potassium glutamate): Combine 10 mL 1M tris acetate (pH 8.2), 14 mL 1M magnesium glutamate, and 60 mL 1M potassium glutamate, then fill to 1 L with deionized water.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh Buffer A with DTT for lysis.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 µL of 1M DTT to 1000 µL Buffer A to reach a final concentration of 2 mM.
Reconstitute LB media from premix per box instructions (alternatively, 2x YTP or 2x YTPG can be used).
Autoclave LB media, tips, and dishes for 20 minutes at 121 °C.

Add 5 mL of LB medium to a culture tube and inoculate with a small amount of bacteria from glycerol stock (e.g., BL21 (DE3), BL21 star (DE3), T7, E. coli RNAP Rosetta (DE3), Top10, Top10-GamS, E. coli RNAP, alpha-complementation M15, or DH5alpha).
Grow overnight in an incubator at 37 °C and 200 RPM with the cap in a loose position for air exchange.

steps.title: Scale Up Culture
steps.instruction: Expand the overnight culture and grow to target density.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of overnight culture to 200 mL of LB medium in a 500 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Measure OD600 of the overnight culture at 10x dilution (100 µL culture in 900 µL LB); expected OD600 is ~4 (0.4 at 10x dilution).
Incubate the culture for 4 hours at 37 °C and 200 RPM until OD600 is ~1.5-2.
If using BL21 (DE3) strains, optionally induce after 2 hours by adding 800 µL of 100 mM IPTG stock (0.4 mM final concentration) to the 200 mL culture.

steps.title: Harvest Bacterial Cells
steps.instruction: Collect and wash the bacterial pellet.

substeps.instruction: As soon as incubation finishes, place the Erlenmeyer flask on ice to arrest growth.
Divide 200 mL of culture into four 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Spin tubes at 4000 rpm (3220g) at 4 °C for 20 minutes using a swing-bucket rotor A-4-62.
Discard supernatant using a pipette and keep the pellet cold on ice.
Add 10 mL of Buffer A (no DTT) to each pellet, resuspend by pipetting, and transfer all four parts into a single, pre-weighed and labeled 50 mL Falcon tube.
Balance the centrifuge with a tube of 40 mL water and spin at 4000 rpm (3220g) at 4 °C for 10 minutes.
Discard supernatant, add 10 mL of Buffer A, and spin again at 4000 rpm (3220g) at 4 °C for 10 minutes. Repeat this spin once more.

steps.title: Determine Wet Mass and Store Cells
steps.instruction: Quantify the cell pellet and preserve if necessary.

substeps.instruction: Weigh the tube containing the pellet (with cap). Calculate wet mass by subtracting the dry weight of the tube recorded earlier (typically ~1 g).
Optionally flash-freeze cells using liquid nitrogen and store at -80 °C.
Keep pellet on ice and add Buffer A with DTT at a ratio of 1 mL buffer per 1 g wet mass.
Resuspend by vortexing and return to ice.
Transfer exactly 1 mL of resuspended cells into a new 2 mL Eppendorf tube.
Place the tube in an ice-water bath.
Immerse the sonicator tip in the tube, ensuring it does not touch the tube surface (drop to bottom and raise slightly).
Sonicate until 400J is achieved, using 50% amplitude and pulses of 10s on / 10s off (typically takes ~1 minute 24 seconds).
Cool the centrifuge (Eppendorf 5424R) to 4 °C using fast temp mode (~20 mins).
Centrifuge the lysate at 12000 x g (11304 rpm) at 4 °C for 10 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube, leaving some lysate behind to avoid bacterial debris.
Place the lysate in an incubator at 37 °C and 200 RPM for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Centrifuge the lysate again at 12000 x g (11304 rpm) at 4 °C for 10 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube, leaving some lysate behind.

steps.title: Aliquot and Store Lysate
steps.instruction: Preserve the final lysate and prepare for assay.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot ~3 µL of lysate into a separate tube for Bradford assay.
Aliquot the remaining lysate into small tubes (recommended ~25 µL per tube) while keeping on ice.
Flash-freeze remaining tubes in liquid nitrogen and store at -80 °C.
Dilute 1 µL of lysate in 99 µL of Buffer A.
Mix 5 µL of this diluted lysate with 250 µL of Bradford reagent.
Incubate for 5 minutes and measure absorbance using a Nanodrop (typical concentration: 40-80 mg/mL).

steps.title: Optional Dialysis
steps.instruction: Perform dialysis if E. coli RNAP is used.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 900 mL of Buffer A + DTT in a 1 L beaker at 4 °C with a magnetic stir bar.
Rehydrate 10k MCWO cassettes in Buffer A + DTT at 4 °C for 2 minutes.
Load cassettes with a maximum of 2.5 mL of extract and dialyze for 3 hours at 4 °C with stirring.
Centrifuge the dialyzed lysate at 12000 x g (11304 rpm) at 4 °C for 10 minutes and transfer the supernatant to a new tube (do not take all lysate).
